Vivek —

Short version: we need ~3 extra weeks of the current pilot window because the usage spike last week burned through our allocated hours. Procurement prefers a short extension rather than moving to a full monthly commitment.

Questions:
- Can Redwood offer a temporary surge patch (time-limited) for the remaining 3 weeks?
- If so, two options we care about: (A) pro‑rated daily extension at the pilot rate, or (B) a burst-credit pack (X tokens/hours) at a small premium. We need pricing and a recommended approach.
- Will there be any SLA changes if we take the burst-credit path?

We also have a lean procurement window — can you send something I can route to legal/finance? Ideally a 1‑page addendum + pricing so we can get an internal PO out.

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on keeping the POC running past the cutoff

Andrew —

Thanks for the context and the usage file — that helps. We can do both patterns; here are two pragmatic options we use for short runway requests: 

Option 1 — Timebox extension (3 weeks):
• Pro‑rated daily extension of the existing pilot rate.
• Includes existing token caps and current model configuration; no SLA change.
• Estimated cost: $9,000 for 21 days (based on your current burn profile).
• Paper: 1‑page addendum (amendment to the pilot agreement).

Option 2 — Burst-credit pack (one‑time):
• Prepaid burst pack equivalent to ~25% additional capacity (tokens/hours).
• 10% premium vs. pro‑rated price to account for on‑demand scheduling.
• Includes an ops playbook and best‑effort priority routing — note: not a guaranteed SLA uplift.
• Estimated cost: $9,900 for the pack.

Recommendations: if you want a clean procurement path and no contract churn, Option 1 is simplest — we email the addendum and you raise the PO. Option 2 is handy if you want to keep the overall end date unchanged but avoid pro‑rata invoicing.

Next steps I can run:
1) Draft the 1‑page addendum for Option 1 and send to Andrew by EOD tomorrow.
2) If you prefer Option 2, I’ll attach the burst pack spec + short SOW and a one‑line acceptance clause.

Marissa — assigning for pricing approval/discount if we want to offer any concession.
Rachel — can you attach the short addendum template and confirm the bill-to flow for a PO?

Onward,
Vivek
Sr. Director, Sales
Redwood Inference
